correctness.rationale: A basis extension gives a bijection from all alternating matrices with prescribed AS=Y to an unconstrained alternating (n-r)x(n-r) block, proving exactly 2^{binom(n-r,2)} completions if S^T Y is alternating. Taking S=1 and then S=[1,d] with exception rank-one d=0 and d=1 yields the exact joint count. Direct orthogonality enumeration gives the marginal law for both parities of n, including n=2. The embedded checker independently exhausts every simple labelled graph through n=6, all state pairs; this is verification, not a replacement for the general proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The fixed-graph automata results have stronger temporal iteration but only special deterministic graph families; they do not imply a distribution under uniform random graph choice. The 2026 Presburger paper is about satisfiability and explicitly leaves modular quantifiers outside its core syntax, so it does not subsume random-model counting.

value.rationale: This is the complete all-n finite-model distribution for the first repeated parity-neighbor update, the first layer at which the graph-generated unary predicate is correlated with the very edges used to aggregate it. It captures a nontrivial orthogonality restriction and isolated atoms, which independent-layer binomial approximations miss. It is a natural complete classification of labelled two-state trajectories usable for any Boolean query on two iterated modular local-count predicates; neither arbitrary slicing nor a routine parameter increment.
